summary: Lewis County, NY: wooden lookout built 1922 by Fisher Forestry on a rock mountain in Watson; NYSFFLA says removed, FFLA lists a standing windmill tower; status unresolved.

facts.design: Wooden tower built 1922 (NYSFFLA); the FFLA list gives the type as Windmill Tower
facts.status_note: NYSFFLA marks the 1922 Rock Mt. tower removed; the FFLA list shows a standing Windmill Tower at the same name and coordinates. Not resolved by any source read.

access.note: Listed among privately owned fire towers (CNY Hiking); no public access described in the sources read

facts.agency: Fisher Forestry and Realty Company, built with Conservation Commission cooperation

events.note: Wooden tower erected by a private Lowville contractor, with Conservation Commission cooperation, as a secondary and emergency station
The 1922 newspaper says the company maintained an observer to watch for fire during dry periods

corrections.why: NYSFFLA marks the 1922 Rock Mt. tower removed; FFLA lists a standing Windmill Tower at the same name and coordinates. The two conflict, and no later source resolves it.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The 1922 newspaper places the tower southeast of Half Moon Lake in Watson; NYSFFLA places it 3 miles southeast of Crystal Lake and the Number Four Road. Both describe the Watson area near Number Four, but they name different landmarks; no map check was done.

notes_for_editor: The main conflict is whether anything stands today. NYSFFLA's Rock Mt. entry (the 1922 wooden tower built by Fisher) says Removed. The FFLA state and county lists show a standing Windmill Tower at 43.81416, -75.23833, under the name Rock Mountain, which may be the same site or a different structure. CNY Hiking's intro names Rock Mountain (Lewis County) among privately owned towers, but its table has no Rock Mountain row, so it is weak support for 'standing'. Brief record said standing; proposed correction to unknown. The 1922 date is consistent across the newspaper transcription and NYSFFLA. Site identity (Rock Mt. = Rock Mountain) is assumed from name and location, not confirmed. Used 2 WebSearch and about 6 page reads, mostly shared lists, which is over the per-tower page budget because of the conflict. No photos found.
